$comment: Generated by scripts/spec/ops.py from the Python registry. Do not edit.

ops.name: A1Z26 decode
ops.description: Split on `delimiter` and write each number from 1 to 26 as a lower-case letter. Spaces, tabs and line breaks around a number are ignored. Anything else is `E_DECODE`.

ops.name: A1Z26 encode
ops.description: Write each ASCII letter as its place in the alphabet (`a` and `A` are 1, `z` and `Z` are 26), joined by `delimiter`. Other characters are dropped.

ops.name: Add line numbers
ops.description: Put the line number and a space before each line, counting from `offset` + 1. Numbers are right-aligned to the width of the line count. A final LF is kept.

ops.name: Adler-32
ops.description: Adler-32 (RFC 1950) as 8 hex digits.

ops.name: AES Decrypt
ops.description: Inverse of `aes-encrypt` with the same arguments. In GCM the last 16 bytes are the tag; a wrong key, IV, AAD or tag raises E_CRYPTO, as does bad PKCS#7 padding.

ops.name: AES Encrypt
ops.description: AES in CBC (default), CTR, GCM or ECB mode. `padding` (PKCS#7 by default) applies to CBC and ECB. In GCM the 16-byte tag is appended and `aad` is authenticated. ECB warns W_INSECURE.

examples.output: b4 dd 38 c9 96 76 b8 ec b1 d3 ad bd 52 ad 57 70

ops.name: Alternating caps
ops.description: Lower-case the first letter, upper-case the next, and so on. Only letters (General_Category L*) take part; other characters are copied and do not break the alternation.

ops.name: Analyse Characters
ops.description: One row per code point (or grapheme cluster) with the columns of PRD §4.6. In grapheme mode `index` is the inclusive code-point range `start-end`, per-code-point values are joined with ` + `, bytes and units with a space, and flags are merged.

examples.output:
index	cp	char	name	gc	block	script	scx	age	bidi	ea	utf8	utf16	decomposition	flags
0	U+0065	e	LATIN SMALL LETTER E	Ll	Basic Latin	Latn	Latn	1.1	L	Na	65	0065		
1	U+0301	◌́	COMBINING ACUTE ACCENT	Mn	Combining Diacritical Marks	Zinh	Cher Cyrl Grek Latn Osge Sunu Tale Todr	1.1	NSM	A	CC 81	0301		
2	U+1F44B	👋	WAVING HAND SIGN	So	Miscellaneous Symbols and Pictographs	Zyyy	Zyyy	6.0	ON	W	F0 9F 91 8B	D83D DC4B		
3	U+1F3FD	🏽	EMOJI MODIFIER FITZPATRICK TYPE-4	Sk	Miscellaneous Symbols and Pictographs	Zyyy	Zyyy	8.0	ON	W	F0 9F 8F BD	D83C DFFD

ops.name: Atbash
ops.description: Mirror the ASCII alphabet (A<->Z, case kept). Other characters are unchanged.

ops.name: Bacon cipher decode
ops.description: Read Bacon codes as upper-case letters. `01` reads `0` and `1`, `ab` reads `A` and `B` in either case, `case` reads lower-case ASCII letters as 0 and upper-case as 1, and `first-letter` reads each word starting with A to M as 0 and N to Z as 1. Other characters are skipped, every five symbols make a letter, and leftover symbols are ignored. A code past the end of the alphabet is written as `?`.

ops.name: Bacon cipher encode
ops.description: Write each ASCII letter as a five-symbol Bacon code. The `standard` alphabet gives I and J one code, and U and V another; `complete` gives all 26 letters their own. Codes are written in `0`/`1` or `A`/`B` and joined by spaces, or, with `keep_other`, written in place among the other characters. `invert` swaps the two symbols.

ops.name: BLAKE2b
ops.description: BLAKE2b (RFC 7693); `size` is the digest length in bytes (1-64, default 64) and `key` an optional key of up to 64 bytes.

ops.name: BLAKE2s
ops.description: BLAKE2s (RFC 7693); `size` is the digest length in bytes (1-32, default 32) and `key` an optional key of up to 32 bytes.

ops.name: Cartesian Product
ops.description: Split the input on `sample_delimiter` into two or more samples and each sample on `item_delimiter` into items. Write every tuple that takes one item from each sample, as `(x,y)` with a comma inside, joined by `item_delimiter`. The last sample varies fastest. At most 100000 tuples.

ops.name: Comment
ops.description: An annotation. The dish passes through unchanged, whatever its type.

ops.name: Conditional jump
ops.description: Jump to the label `to` when `pattern` matches the dish (or does not, with `invert`), at most `max` times; then continue with a W_JUMP_LIMIT warning.

ops.name: Count
ops.description: Count bytes, or decode UTF-8 (U+FFFD for ill-formed input) and count UTF-16 units, code points, grapheme clusters or lines (LF-separated; a final LF does not start a new line).

ops.name: CRC-32
ops.description: CRC-32 (ISO-HDLC, as in zlib and PNG) as 8 hex digits.

examples.input: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog

ops.name: CSV to JSON
ops.description: Parse RFC 4180 CSV. With `header`, the first record names the fields of an object per record; otherwise each record is an array. Cells stay strings.

ops.name: Decode Text
ops.description: Decode bytes from a character encoding. Ill-formed input becomes U+FFFD.

ops.name: Detect Confusables
ops.description: UTS #39 skeletons (NFD, confusables.txt, NFD). With a `reference`, one row compares both skeletons (code points as hex) and `confusable` is `true` when they are equal. Without one, one row per code point that has a confusables.txt prototype.

examples.output:
index	cp	name	prototype
1	U+0430	CYRILLIC SMALL LETTER A	U+0061

ops.name: Detect Invisible Characters
ops.description: One row per invisible code point: bidi controls (Trojan Source, CVE-2021-42574), tag characters, variation selectors, zero-width characters, Hangul fillers and other default-ignorables. `index` is the 0-based code-point offset; `line` and `column` are 1-based, lines are LF-separated and columns count code points.

examples.output:
index	cp	name	kind	line	column
1	U+200B	ZERO WIDTH SPACE	zero-width	1	2
3	U+2060	WORD JOINER	zero-width	1	4

ops.name: Encode Text
ops.description: Encode text in a character encoding. Lone surrogates become U+FFFD; no BOM.

ops.name: Escape Smart Characters
ops.description: Replace typographic characters (curly quotes, dashes, ellipsis, ©, ®, ™, arrows and some spaces) with plain ASCII. Other non-ASCII characters are kept (`include`), removed (`remove`) or replaced with a dot (`replace`).

ops.name: Escape String
ops.description: Escape a string for a JavaScript literal the way jsesc does. `special` escapes all but printable ASCII, `everything` escapes every character and `minimal` only the quote, backslash, control escapes and line or paragraph separators. `json` uses \u escapes and wraps the result in quotes; `es6` writes characters past U+FFFF as \u{...}.

ops.name: Escape Unicode
ops.description: Write characters as escapes with upper-case hex. `scope` picks every non-ASCII character, every character, or only non-printable ones (categories C, Zl, Zp, Zs other than U+0020, and default-ignorables). `backslash-u` and `percent-u` write astral characters as surrogate pairs.

ops.name: Filter by Property
ops.description: Keep or remove the code points whose property has one of the comma-separated `value`s. Names and aliases match loosely (`L`, `Letter`, `Latn`, `Basic Latin`); a General_Category group such as `L` covers its members.

ops.name: Find / replace
ops.description: Replace matches of `pattern` with `replacement`. As a regex, the replacement uses JavaScript syntax: `$$`, `$&`, `$1`-`$99` and `$<name>`; empty matches are replaced too. With `literal`, both are plain text and the pattern must not be empty.

ops.name: Fork
ops.description: Split the input on `split`, run `steps` on each part, and join the results with `merge`. An error in any branch fails the fork; its path names the branch.

ops.name: From Base
ops.description: Read a number written in a radix from 2 to 36 and write it in decimal. Digits are case-insensitive, whitespace is ignored and a leading + or - is allowed. A fraction gets at most 20 decimal places, rounded half up.

ops.name: From Base32
ops.description: Decode Base32. Without `strict`, it is case-insensitive and skips other characters.

ops.name: From Base45
ops.description: Decode Base45 (RFC 9285). Without `strict`, it skips characters outside the alphabet.

ops.name: From Base58
ops.description: Decode Base58. Without `strict`, it skips characters outside the alphabet.

ops.name: From Base62
ops.description: Decode a base-62 number to bytes. Without `strict`, it skips other characters.

ops.name: From Base64
ops.description: Decode Base64. Without `strict`, characters outside the alphabet are skipped.

ops.name: From Base85
ops.description: Decode Ascii85 (optionally inside `<~ ~>`) or Z85. Without `strict`, it skips characters outside the alphabet.

ops.name: From Base92
ops.description: Decode Base92. Without `strict`, it skips characters outside the alphabet.

ops.name: From BCD
ops.description: Read binary-coded decimal back into a decimal integer. The input is binary digits (`nibbles` or `bytes`, spaces ignored) or one character per byte (`raw`). With `signed`, the last nibble is the sign: 1101 or 1011 is minus.

ops.name: From Bech32
ops.description: Check the checksum of a Bech32 or Bech32m string and write its data as hex. A SegWit address gives the witness version byte and then the program. Other formats: `raw` (one character per byte), `script-pubkey`, `hrp-hex` and `json`.

ops.name: From Binary
ops.description: Read bytes of 1-8 binary digits. `auto` splits on runs of whitespace and ,:; and `none` reads groups of exactly eight digits.

ops.name: From Braille
ops.description: Replace each six-dot Braille pattern (U+2800 to U+283F) with its North American Braille ASCII character; letters come out in upper case. Other characters are copied.

ops.name: From Charcode
ops.description: Read code points written in `base` and separated by `delimiter`. Whitespace around each code is ignored and empty codes are skipped.

ops.name: From Code Points
ops.description: Read code points separated by whitespace, commas or semicolons. A `U+` or `0x` prefix always means hex; bare numbers use `base`. Surrogates are kept as code points (they become U+FFFD if the dish is later used as text).

ops.name: From Decimal
ops.description: Read bytes of 1-3 decimal digits (at most 255). `auto` splits on runs of whitespace and ,:;

ops.name: From Float
ops.description: Read decimal numbers separated by `delimiter` and write each as an IEEE 754 `float` (4 bytes) or `double` (8 bytes), rounded to the nearest value. `Infinity`, `-Infinity` and `NaN` are accepted.

ops.name: From Hex
ops.description: Read hex digit pairs. `auto` strips 0x and \x prefixes, whitespace and ,:;-.

ops.name: From Hex Content
ops.description: Read Snort content: hex between pipes becomes those bytes and the rest is UTF-8.

ops.name: From Hexdump
ops.description: Read the bytes back from a hexdump in the xxd, hexdump -C, Wireshark or 010 Editor style: on each line, an optional offset and then the hex columns. Check the result.

ops.name: From Modhex
ops.description: Read Modhex digit pairs, in either case, ignoring whitespace. `auto` also drops every other character; any other choice removes only that delimiter.

ops.name: From Morse code
ops.description: Read International Morse code. Dashes may be `-`, `_`, hyphens, en or em dashes or the word `dash`; dots may be `.`, `·` or the word `dot`. Words are split on `word_delimiter` and joined with a space; a code that is not in the table is dropped.

ops.name: From Octal
ops.description: Read bytes of 1-3 octal digits (at most 377). `auto` splits on runs of whitespace and ,:; and `none` reads groups of exactly three digits.

ops.name: From Punycode
ops.description: Decode Punycode (RFC 3492). With `domain`, split the input into labels as to-punycode does and decode each label that starts with xn-- (any case).

ops.name: Generate Random Bytes
ops.description: Replace the input with `length` random bytes: from the platform's secure random generator, or, when the recipe has a `seed`, from SHA-256 in counter mode.

ops.name: Get all casings
ops.description: Every combination of upper and lower case, one per line. The input is lower-cased, then line k upper-cases the code points whose bit is set in k (the first code point is bit 0). At most 16 code points.

ops.name: Grapheme Split
ops.description: Join the extended grapheme clusters (UAX #29) with `delimiter`.

ops.name: Gunzip
ops.description: Decompress gzip data (RFC 1952), member after member, checking each CRC-32 and length. Anything after the last member that is not another member is an error.

ops.name: Gzip
ops.description: Compress to one gzip member (RFC 1952) with no file name, a zero modification time and OS 255 (unknown), so the output does not depend on when or where it is made.

ops.name: Hamming Distance
ops.description: Split the input on `delimiter` into two samples of equal length, read as UTF-8 text or as hex (whitespace ignored). Write the number of positions where they differ, counting bytes or bits.

ops.name: Head
ops.description: The first `count` lines (keeping a final LF), graphemes or code points.

ops.name: Hex to PEM
ops.description: Write hex bytes (usually DER) as a PEM block: a BEGIN line with the `header` label, the bytes as Base64 in lines of 64 characters, and an END line. Lines end in CR LF.

ops.name: HMAC
ops.description: HMAC (RFC 2104) with `hash` (default sha256) and a bytes `key`.

ops.name: HTML Entity Decode
ops.description: Decode named and numeric character references as HTML does in text content: the longest known name wins, legacy names may omit the semicolon, numeric references may omit it, 0x80-0x9F map through windows-1252, and 0, surrogates and values above 10FFFF become U+FFFD. An `&` that starts no reference stays as it is. `strict` fails on a missing semicolon, an unknown name or an invalid code point instead.

ops.name: HTML Entity Encode
ops.description: Replace characters with references. `scope` is the five HTML-special characters `& < > " '`, those plus every non-ASCII character, or all characters. `named` uses the shortest name ending in `;` (hex where there is none); astral characters get one reference each.

ops.name: IDNA To ASCII
ops.description: UTS #46 ToASCII with nontransitional processing: map, normalise to NFC, check every label, and encode non-ASCII labels as xn-- plus Punycode. Any error fails the op with E_DECODE, naming the first error found. `verify_dns_length` requires labels of 1 to 63 characters and a name of 1 to 253 (not counting a final dot).

ops.name: IDNA To Unicode
ops.description: UTS #46 ToUnicode with nontransitional processing: map, normalise to NFC, decode xn-- labels and check every label. Any error fails the op with E_DECODE, naming the first error found.

ops.name: Join lines
ops.description: Join the lines with `delimiter`. A final LF is dropped.

ops.name: JSON Beautify
ops.description: Write JSON with one value per line, like `JSON.stringify(v, null, indent)`. `sort_keys` orders object keys by code point.

ops.name: JSON Minify
ops.description: Write JSON with no whitespace, keeping key order.

ops.name: JSON to CSV
ops.description: Write an array of objects (with a header row) or an array of arrays as CSV. Every record ends with the line ending.

ops.name: Jump
ops.description: Jump to the label `to`, at most `max` times; then continue with a W_JUMP_LIMIT warning. Every jump counts towards the step limit.

ops.name: JWT Decode
ops.description: Split a JWT into `header`, `payload` and `signature` (base64url text), without checking the signature or time claims. Surrounding whitespace is ignored.

ops.name: JWT Sign
ops.description: Sign a JSON object as a JWT. `key` is the HMAC secret for HS*, or a PEM/DER private key. `header` adds JSON fields after `alg` and `typ` ("JWT"); it may replace `typ` but not `alg`. PS* and ES* signatures are randomised; `none` warns W_INSECURE.

ops.name: JWT Verify
ops.description: Check a JWT's signature and return its payload. The header `alg` must equal `algorithm` (so `none` and algorithm swaps are refused). `key` is the HMAC secret, or a PEM/DER public key, certificate or private key. Tokens with `crit` are refused. Time claims (`exp`, `nbf`) are not checked. Failures raise E_CRYPTO.

ops.name: Label
ops.description: A jump target. The dish passes through unchanged, whatever its type.

ops.name: Leet speak
ops.description: `to` replaces the ASCII letters a, e, i, o, s and t, in either case, with 4, 3, 1, 0, 5 and 7. `from` replaces those digits with the lower-case letters. Other characters are copied.

ops.name: Levenshtein Distance
ops.description: Split the input on `delimiter` into two samples. Write the least total cost of the insertions, deletions and substitutions of characters (code points) that turn the first sample into the second. The product of the two lengths may be at most 4000000.

ops.name: MD5
ops.description: MD5 digest (RFC 1321). Warns W_INSECURE.

ops.name: Normalize
ops.description: Apply a Unicode normalization form (UAX #15) from the pinned UCD.

ops.name: Pad lines
ops.description: Add `length` code points to the start or end of each line, made by repeating `character` and cutting it to length. A final LF is kept.

ops.name: Parse Query String
ops.description: Split `name=value` pairs on `&` and percent-decode them as UTF-8. A leading `?` is ignored. In `object` output a repeated name collects its values into an array.

ops.name: Parse URL
ops.description: Split a URL into its RFC 3986 parts without decoding or normalising them. An absent part is null; surrounding ASCII whitespace is ignored.

ops.name: PBKDF2
ops.description: Derive a `length`-byte key from the input password (PBKDF2-HMAC, RFC 8018) and return it as hex. Warns W_INSECURE below 100 000 iterations.

ops.name: PEM to Hex
ops.description: Find each PEM block (BEGIN and END lines with the same label), decode its Base64 body and write the bytes as hex, one line per block.

ops.name: Power Set
ops.description: Split the input on `item_delimiter` into items, dropping empty ones and repeats. Write every subset on its own line, items joined by `item_delimiter` and each line ending in a line feed: the empty set first, then smaller subsets before larger ones, and subsets of one size in input order. At most 16 items.

ops.name: Quoted-Printable Decode
ops.description: Decode quoted-printable. Soft line breaks and trailing spaces are removed, and other line breaks are kept as they are. Without `strict`, lower-case hex is accepted and a stray `=` is kept.

ops.name: Quoted-Printable Encode
ops.description: Encode bytes as quoted-printable, with lines of at most 76 characters. In `text` mode, LF and CRLF are line breaks, written as CRLF; in `binary` mode they are escaped.

ops.name: Raw Deflate
ops.description: Compress to a raw DEFLATE stream (RFC 1951) with no header or checksum. Level 0 stores the input uncompressed; 1 is fastest and 9 smallest.

ops.name: Raw Inflate
ops.description: Decompress a raw DEFLATE stream (RFC 1951). The stream must be complete, and no bytes may follow it.

ops.name: Regex extract
ops.description: List every match of `pattern` (or its capture group `group`), joined by `separator`. Empty matches count; a group that did not participate gives "".

ops.name: Remove ANSI escape codes
ops.description: Remove ANSI control sequences (ESC `[`, parameter bytes, intermediate bytes and a final byte), such as colour and cursor codes.

ops.name: Remove Bidi Controls
ops.description: Delete every Bidi_Control character (U+061C, U+200E, U+200F, U+202A..U+202E, U+2066..U+2069).

ops.name: Remove line numbers
ops.description: At the start of each line, remove up to five spaces or tabs, ASCII digits and one following separator: whitespace (including a line feed) or one of `:|-,.)]`.

ops.name: Remove null bytes
ops.description: Remove every 0x00 byte.

ops.name: Reverse
ops.description: Reverse the order of graphemes (default), code points or bytes. The first two decode UTF-8 first, replacing ill-formed sequences with U+FFFD.

ops.name: ROT13
ops.description: Rotate ASCII letters by `amount` (default 13, case kept); with `digits`, also rotate 0-9 by the same amount mod 10. Other characters are unchanged.

ops.name: ROT47
ops.description: Rotate printable ASCII U+0021..U+007E by `amount` (default 47) mod 94.

ops.name: ROT8000
ops.description: Rotate visible Basic Multilingual Plane characters halfway through the list of 63 404 that take part, so applying it twice gives the input back. Spaces, controls and characters outside the BMP are copied.

examples.output: 籑籮籵籵籸簵 籠籸类籵籭簪

ops.name: Script Mix Check
ops.description: The UTS #39 restriction level of the whole input: ASCII-Only, Single Script, Highly Restrictive, Moderately Restrictive, Minimally Restrictive or Unrestricted. `profile` (default true) applies step 1, so characters that are not Identifier_Status=Allowed (including spaces and punctuation) give Unrestricted.

ops.name: Set Difference
ops.description: Split the input on `sample_delimiter` into two samples and each sample on `item_delimiter` into items. Write the items of the first sample that are not in the second, once, in their order.

ops.name: Set Intersection
ops.description: Split the input on `sample_delimiter` into two samples and each sample on `item_delimiter` into items. Write the items that are in both samples, once, in the order of the first sample.

ops.name: Set Union
ops.description: Split the input on `sample_delimiter` into two samples and each sample on `item_delimiter` into items. Write every item that is in either sample, once, in the order first seen.

ops.name: SHA-1
ops.description: SHA-1 digest (FIPS 180-4). Warns W_INSECURE.

ops.name: SHA-3
ops.description: SHA-3 digest (FIPS 202); `size` is 256 (default), 224, 384 or 512.

ops.name: SHAKE
ops.description: SHAKE extendable-output function (FIPS 202); `size` is 128 (default) or 256 and `length` is the output length in bytes (default 32).

ops.name: Show Bidi Classes
ops.description: One row per code point with its Bidi_Class (short and long name) and whether it is Bidi_Mirrored. Controls and invisible characters are shown by name.

examples.output:
index	cp	char	bidi	bidi_name	mirrored
0	U+0061	a	L	Left_To_Right	false
1	U+202E	⟨RIGHT-TO-LEFT OVERRIDE⟩	RLO	Right_To_Left_Override	false
2	U+0628	ب	AL	Arabic_Letter	false
3	U+0028	(	ON	Other_Neutral	true
4	U+0031	1	EN	European_Number	false

ops.name: Sort lines
ops.description: Stable sort of the lines. `code-point` compares code points; `case-insensitive` compares full case folds; `numeric` compares a leading decimal number, with lines that have none after the rest; `length` counts code points. `descending` reverses the order of the keys, keeping equal lines in input order.

ops.name: Split
ops.description: Split on the literal `delimiter` and join the parts with `join`.

ops.name: Strip Diacritics
ops.description: NFD, then drop nonspacing marks that are Diacritic and of the Inherited script, then NFC. Script-specific marks such as the Devanagari virama are kept, and letters with no decomposition (ø, ł) are unchanged.

ops.name: Strip HTML tags
ops.description: Remove everything from `<` to the next `>`, repeating until none is left. Then `remove_indentation` drops spaces and tabs after each line feed, and `remove_line_breaks` drops a blank first line and folds runs of blank lines into one line feed. The result is text, not safe HTML.

ops.name: Sub-recipe
ops.description: Run `steps` as one group. The runner keeps the dish type across the group; this function serves direct calls only.

ops.name: Subsection
ops.description: Run `steps` on each match of `pattern` (or on its capture group `group`) and splice the results back; the rest of the dish passes through. Empty matches and groups that did not participate are left alone. With `global` off, only the first match is used. An error inside a match fails the step; its path names the match.

ops.name: Swap case
ops.description: Upper-case every character that changes when upper-cased, and lower-case the rest, one code point at a time with full case mappings (`ß` becomes `SS`).

ops.name: Swap Endianness
ops.description: Reverse the byte order inside each word of `word_length` bytes. With `hex`, the input is hex text (as From Hex reads it with `auto`) and the output is space-separated lower-case hex. With `pad`, a short final word is filled with zero bytes first.

ops.name: Symmetric Difference
ops.description: Split the input on `sample_delimiter` into two samples and each sample on `item_delimiter` into items. Write the items that are in exactly one sample, once: those of the first sample, then those of the second.

ops.name: Tail
ops.description: The last `count` lines (keeping a final LF), graphemes or code points.

ops.name: Text-Integer Conversion
ops.description: Convert between text and the big-endian integer its bytes spell: `ABC` is 0x414243 is 4276803. Input that is all digits is read as decimal, input starting with 0x as hex and anything else, quoted or not, as text. `output` picks the form to write.

ops.name: To Base
ops.description: Write a decimal number in a radix from 2 to 36 with lower-case digits. A fraction gets at most 20 digits, rounded half up.

ops.name: To Base32
ops.description: Encode bytes as Base32 (RFC 4648 §6) or base32hex (§7).

ops.name: To Base45
ops.description: Encode bytes as Base45 (RFC 9285), the QR-code encoding: 2 bytes become 3 characters.

ops.name: To Base58
ops.description: Encode bytes as Base58. Each leading zero byte becomes the alphabet's first digit.

ops.name: To Base62
ops.description: Write the bytes, read as one big-endian number, in base 62. Leading zeros are not kept.

ops.name: To Base64
ops.description: Encode bytes as Base64 (RFC 4648 §4 or §5, or a custom alphabet).

ops.name: To Base85
ops.description: Encode bytes as Ascii85 (`z` for a group of four zero bytes) or Z85.

ops.name: To Base92
ops.description: Encode bytes as Base92: every 13 bits become two printable ASCII characters.

ops.name: To BCD
ops.description: Write a decimal integer as binary-coded decimal: four bits per digit in the chosen `scheme`. `packed` puts two digits in a byte, `signed` adds a sign nibble (1100 plus, 1101 minus) at the end, and `format` shows nibbles, bytes or one character per byte.

ops.name: To Bech32
ops.description: Encode bytes as Bech32 or Bech32m: the human-readable part `hrp`, a `1`, the data in a 32-character alphabet and a six-character checksum. `segwit` mode writes a Bitcoin SegWit address from a witness program and `witness_version`.

ops.name: To Binary
ops.description: Write each byte as eight binary digits, separated by `delimiter`.

ops.name: To Braille
ops.description: Replace each character of North American Braille ASCII (space, ASCII letters in either case, digits and `!"#$%&'()*+,-./:;<=>?@[\]^_`) with its six-dot Braille pattern, U+2800 to U+283F. Other characters are copied.

ops.name: To Camel case
ops.description: Like To Snake case, but the first word is lower case and every later word is title case, with nothing between them.

ops.name: To Charcode
ops.description: Write each code point in `base`. Base 16 pads to 2, 4 or 6 digits; other bases do not pad.

ops.name: To Code Points
ops.description: Write each code point as `U+0041`, `0041`, `0x0041` or `65`.

ops.name: To Decimal
ops.description: Write each byte as a decimal number without padding, separated by `delimiter`.

ops.name: To Float
ops.description: Read the bytes as IEEE 754 numbers, 4 bytes each for `float` or 8 for `double`, and write them in decimal joined by `delimiter`. Each number is written with the fewest digits that give the same value back.

ops.name: To Hex
ops.description: Write each byte as two hex digits, separated or prefixed by `delimiter`.

ops.name: To Hex Content
ops.description: Write bytes as Snort content: ASCII letters, digits and spaces stay as they are and every other byte goes between pipes as hex. `special-and-space` also converts spaces, `all` converts everything, and `spaces` puts a space between hex bytes.

ops.name: To Hexdump
ops.description: Write `width` bytes per line: the offset, the bytes in hex and the bytes as Latin-1 text, with controls and the soft hyphen as dots (`ascii_only` keeps only printable ASCII). `final_length` adds a last line with the total length.

ops.name: To Kebab case
ops.description: Like To Snake case, but the words are joined with hyphens.

ops.name: To Modhex
ops.description: Write each byte as two Modhex digits, separated by `delimiter`. With `bytes_per_line`, a line feed follows the delimiter after every that many bytes.

ops.name: To Morse code
ops.description: Write each character as International Morse code. Letters are joined by `letter_delimiter` and words (split on runs of spaces) by `word_delimiter`; lines stay on their own lines. A character with no code is written as nothing but still gets its delimiters.

ops.name: To NATO alphabet
ops.description: Replace each ASCII letter, digit, `,`, `/` and `.` with its NATO spelling word and a space. Other characters are copied.

ops.name: To Octal
ops.description: Write each byte as three octal digits, separated by `delimiter`.

ops.name: To Punycode
ops.description: Encode the input with Punycode (RFC 3492). With `domain`, split it into labels at full stops (U+002E, U+3002, U+FF0E, U+FF61), encode each label that has a non-ASCII character as xn-- plus Punycode, and join the labels with U+002E. No mapping or checks are applied; use idna-to-ascii for that.

ops.name: To Snake case
ops.description: Split the text into words and join them in lower case with underscores. Words are runs of letters, marks and numbers, split where lower case meets upper case, before the last capital of an acronym and between letters and numbers; apostrophes are dropped. With `context_aware`, only identifiers outside double-quoted strings change.

ops.name: Trim
ops.description: Remove White_Space characters from the start, end or both ends of the text, or of every line with `lines` (a final LF is kept).

ops.name: Unescape String
ops.description: Replace backslash escapes: \n \r \t \b \f \v \a, quotes and backslash, octal \nnn, hex \xnn, \unnnn (surrogate pairs combine) and \u{n...}. Other backslashes stay as they are.

ops.name: Unescape Unicode
ops.description: Replace escapes with characters; `all` recognises every format. Adjacent UTF-16 escapes of one format combine into a pair; a lone surrogate becomes U+FFFD, and an escape above 10FFFF is left as it is.

ops.name: Unicode Case
ops.description: Full case mapping with Final_Sigma and the `tr`, `az` and `lt` tailorings. `fold` is full case folding, or simple folding with `simple` (ignored by other modes).

ops.name: Unique lines
ops.description: Keep the first of each set of equal lines, in input order. `ignore_case` compares full case folds; `count` prefixes each line with its number of copies and a tab.

ops.name: URL Decode
ops.description: Decode %XX escapes; malformed escapes stay as they are. Never fails.

ops.name: URL Encode
ops.description: Percent-encode with upper-case hex over the UTF-8 bytes of the input.

ops.name: UTF-8 Explain
ops.description: One row per byte: its bits, its role in the UTF-8 structure and, on the first byte of each sequence, the code point it encodes. Ill-formed input decodes to U+FFFD by maximal subparts, as everywhere else, and `note` says why.

examples.output:
offset	byte	bits	role	cp	char	note
0	C3	11000011	lead of 2	U+00E9	é	
1	A9	10101001	continuation			
2	E2	11100010	lead of 3	U+20AC	€	
3	82	10000010	continuation			
4	AC	10101100	continuation

ops.name: Vigenère Decode
ops.description: Undo `vigenere-encode`: shift each ASCII letter back by the next letter of `key`.

ops.name: Vigenère Encode
ops.description: Shift each ASCII letter forward by the next letter of `key` (A=0, case kept). Other characters are unchanged and do not use up a key letter.

ops.name: Wrap
ops.description: Break each line into lines of at most `width` characters. Existing line breaks, blank lines and a CR before a line feed are kept.

ops.name: XOR
ops.description: XOR with a repeating `key`. `rolling` adds the number of completed passes over the key to each key byte (mod 256), so the key stream changes on every pass. Both schemes are their own inverse.

ops.name: Zlib Deflate
ops.description: Compress to the zlib format (RFC 1950): a 2-byte header, raw DEFLATE and an Adler-32 checksum.

ops.name: Zlib Inflate
ops.description: Decompress zlib data (RFC 1950) and check its Adler-32. A preset dictionary is not supported, and no bytes may follow the checksum.
